title: Every Plant-Based Food Tested Had a Fungal Toxin — but Don't Panic
summary:
Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods and drinks — and every single one contained at least one fungal toxin. The products included vegan burgers, vegan sausages, and oat, almond and soy milk sold in the UK.

The toxins are called mycotoxins. They are poisonous substances made by certain fungi, including molds. They can get into food when crops are contaminated while growing, being harvested or stored.

Before you panic, here is the reassuring part. Every product contained mycotoxin levels below the European Union's recommended guideline levels.

Mycotoxins are chemicals, not living mold, so finding one does not automatically mean a food is unsafe. The risk depends on the type of toxin, how much is present and how much a person eats over time.

The bigger question is repeated exposure. Earlier studies suggest that small amounts eaten regularly may add up over time. But the new findings do not show that the tested products cause these problems.

'Mycotoxins occur naturally in foods and cannot be completely avoided,' said Andrea Patriarca of Cranfield University. 'As consumers, we should not be frightened.'
why_it_matters: If you eat plant-based foods, it is good to know what is in them — and that the levels found were safe.

background_read: Fungi are living things that include mushrooms and molds, and some of them make poisonous substances called mycotoxins.
These toxins can get into crops while they are growing or being stored, and from there into the foods made from those crops.
Food safety experts set safe limits, and food is tested to check it stays below those limits.
